statusNote: Single source of truth for every FastPay EIP-712 type string. NOT FROZEN: freeze condition C-11 (EIP-712 types frozen) needs the Wallet Protocol Engineer and the Solidity Lead to approve this file (evidence/freeze_register.json). Strings marked QUOTED are copied from the cited document; DERIVED strings were assembled by the implementer from the field lists of the cited documents (they close FZ-22 and PR-10 as a proposal, not as a decision).

MAX_WITNESS_BATCH.record: 10 section 8 question 2 (not a PC record: merchant and fee, Router v1.0)
MAX_WITNESS_BATCH.appliesTo: the batch witness transfer of Pay Once

MAX_EXPOSED_TOKENS_PER_ROUTER.appliesTo: the exposure index of one (customer, router): not a typed-data bound, shared by the manager and the successor validator

MAX_SIGNERS_PER_SET.appliesTo: the members of one quote-signer set: not a typed-data bound, used by SignerSetRegistry

structs.name: FiatTerms
structs.source: 11 section 3 (FiatCaps); 12 section 5.3.2; ADR-020 (the price band is not in the mandate: it is the entry (token, currency, boundsVersion) of the bounds registry)
structs.note: `currency` is the invoice currency (ISO 4217 numeric) and `boundsVersion` the version of the price-bounds registry that the mandate pins; the band [minPriceE18, maxPriceE18] of each (token, currency, boundsVersion) is read from the registry, which never changes a published version (ADR-020).

structs.name: MandateTerms
structs.note: hashStruct(MandateTerms) is `termsHash` of 12 section 5.3 (predicate A3: auth.newTermsHash = termsHash(N)). It holds everything the customer can compare; `accountPin`, the router and the identifiers are outside it.

structs.name: ActivationTerms
structs.source: 17 section 5.3 names it; field list assembled from 11 section 3.1 and 12 section 5.3
structs.note: creationNonce is the replay protection: lineageId = keccak256(abi.encode(LINEAGE_TAG, chainId, mandateManager, customer, merchantId, subscriptionRef, creationNonce)) exists once.

structs.name: RevokeMandate
structs.source: 06 section 3 and 17 section 5.4 name revokeBySig; fields are the minimum that identifies the act
structs.note: Revoking the active mandate of a lineage terminates the lineage (12 section 5.2, T8). Exits are never gated by the signature mode (17 section 5.4).

structs.name: PauseMandate
structs.note: Sets the customer pause bit only; the risk and delegation bits are not the customer's to set or clear. Exits are never gated by the signature mode.

structs.name: ResumeMandate
structs.note: Clears the customer pause bit only; it grants nothing the mandate did not already have, and AUTH uses the pin already stored (17 section 5.4).

structs.name: ReduceMandate
structs.note: oldTermsHash must equal the stored termsHash (a stale reduction is refused); newTermsHash = hashStruct(MandateTerms) of the narrower terms, which the caller supplies as calldata and which must satisfy Contained(new, snapshot(old)) (12 section 5.3.2). Widening is not expressible: it is a REVISION.

structs.name: PayOnceIntent
structs.note: Signed as the witness of a Permit2 SignatureTransfer: the domain is Permit2's own (name Permit2, no version), see `permit2Witness`.

permit2Witness.source: Uniswap/permit2 cc306b601f172c51bc04334a109e98340456620b: src/libraries/PermitHash.sol (the stubs) and src/interfaces/ISignatureTransfer.sol
permit2Witness.rule: witnessTypeString = '<WitnessType> witness)' + encodeType(<WitnessType>) with the referenced types appended in alphabetical order: the witness struct first, TokenPermissions after it (P < T). Permit2 hashes stub ++ witnessTypeString and does not check the string, so a wrong string only makes the signature fail; the router must hard-code it.

snapshotEncoding.status: PROPOSED (revision of the encoding of the reference model: adds customer, anchorStartsAt and boundsVersion, removes the price pair, orders the caps as the typed data; findings F-06, F-07, F-09)
snapshotEncoding.source: tools/eip712_vectors.py snapshot_hash reads this list; FastPayTypes.snapshotHash and fastpay-types.generated.ts are generated from it; 12 section 5.3.2
snapshotEncoding.rule: termsSnapshotHash = keccak256(abi.encode(w1, ..., wN)) over the words below, in this order; every word is one 32-byte value. `arg:` words are the arguments of the function (the identifiers of the lineage and of the predecessor, the generation, the customer), `terms:` words are fields of MandateTerms (and `terms.fiat:` of its FiatTerms), SNAPSHOT_TAG is keccak256 of the tag string. `digest:tokens` is keccak256 of the 32-byte words of the token addresses in the order of the terms (strictly ascending, TermsShape); `digest:capTable` is keccak256 of the concatenation, token by token in the same order, of the token word and the six cap words perPaymentMax, dayMax, weekMax, thirtyDayMax, periodMax, totalMax (the order of TokenTerms).

versioning.status: PROPOSED (part of the freeze fingerprint: an approval of the types is an approval of this policy)
rules: V1 The domain version string identifies the whole message set of a domain (`FastPay Mandates`, `FastPay Quote`). Any change to a type string, to a domain name, to the snapshot encoding or to a tag that a signature covers is a new domain version, deployed as new contracts; the previous contracts, and every signature made for them, are unchanged and cannot be replayed on the new domain because the domain separator differs.
V2 A deployed contract supports exactly one domain version and one type string per message: there is no version negotiation, no fallback and no upgrade of a type string in place.

V3 A type that is used inside a Permit2 witness is never edited: a changed `PayOnceIntent` is a new type with a new name (`PayOnceIntentV2`) under a new router address, so a signature for one can never validate on the other (09 section 5).

V4 The snapshot encoding is versioned by its tag (`fastpay.migration.snapshot.v1`); changing a word, its order or its source is `.v2` and is a domain version change under V1, because `termsSnapshotHash` is signed.

V5 The price-bounds registry is append-only: a published (token, currency, boundsVersion) entry is never changed or removed, so a mandate that pins a version always reads the band that its customer was shown. A new band is a new version.
V6 Every change under V1 to V5 goes through the Freeze Change Request of 14 section 7 and re-derives the freeze fingerprint; an approval names the fingerprint it approves.
